findings.headline: 99215 on 31.9% of 2,372 claims vs 6.7% expected; 8/30 random charts below billed (6 of 9 documented 99215s)
findings.interpretation: Billed far above peers at every complexity level, including 21.8% 99215 on patients with no chronic conditions (peers 3.6%). Random sample of 30 charts, all usable: 26.7% support a lower level than billed. Note rates are near baseline, so the notes do not look inflated; this is a billing-level mismatch. Overpayment estimate from the random sample is about $24,655 (CI $14,658 to $34,653). Data quality clean. Draft summary passed the citation check. For human coder review, not a finding.

findings.headline: 99215 at 4.3x expected on a low-complexity panel; 13 of 43 reviewed charts below billed
findings.interpretation: 54% of visits are on low-complexity patients, and 99215 shares are 14 to 29% where peers bill 4 to 8%. The chart rule triggered at a 30% below-billed rate. 28 of 30 random charts were usable (2 illegible). Estimate about $1,871 (CI $1,132 to $2,610). Small practice, so the dollars are modest. Data quality clean.

findings.headline: 99215 on 33% of claims; 10 of 47 reviewed charts below billed
findings.interpretation: The panel is sicker than average (only 10% low complexity), but 99215 shares are above peers in every stratum. After a follow-up, all 30 random charts came back; the chart rule triggered at a 21% below-billed rate. Estimate about $2,564 (CI $1,755 to $3,373). A partly sicker panel may explain some of the excess. Coder review recommended.

After a follow-up, all 30 random charts came back; the chart rule triggered at a 21% below-billed rate. Estimate about $2564 (CI $1755 to $3373). A partly sicker panel may explain some of the excess. Coder review recommended.

findings.headline: High 99215 share, concentrated in patients with 5+ conditions; 0 of 29 charts below billed
findings.interpretation: Only 4% low-complexity visits. Its 99215 claims cluster in patients with 5+ conditions. After a follow-up, 29 random charts all supported the billed level, and note signals were near baseline.

findings.headline: Sick panel (6% low complexity); 2 of 30 charts below billed
findings.interpretation: Documentation supports the billed levels; note signals near baseline. The 99215 share within each complexity stratum is still above peers, so it is worth routine monitoring only.

findings.headline: 2.25x expected; 3 of 30 charts below billed
findings.interpretation: Documentation largely supports billing. The duplicate-note rate (27%) is notable, but rates are not proof.

findings.headline: 2.66x expected; 4 of 29 charts below billed (14%), well below the peer comparison rate
findings.interpretation: The hybrid review found the documentation supports the billed levels. One note was unsigned.

findings.headline: 99215 at 3.55x expected, but only 1 of 30 random charts below billed
findings.interpretation: Charts support the levels billed, and note signals are at baseline rates (problems 10%, data 10%, late 10%). Yet the 99215 share at 1 to 4 conditions is well above peers (for example 19.2% vs 5.6% at one condition). Documentation inflation can't be ruled out without an audit trail, but there is no positive evidence of it. Not referred for recovery.

findings.headline: 99215 at 4.38x expected; 3 of 45 charts (random plus targeted 99215) below billed
findings.interpretation: Charts mostly support the billed level, but 33% of notes address fewer problems than the claimed level implies, and 35% of 2-condition visits are billed 99215 (peers 8%). This may be notes written to match the bill; an audit trail or coder review would be the next step. Not enough for an upcoding leaning.

findings.headline: 99215 at 5.71x expected on an 80% low-complexity panel; only 12 of 30 charts returned
findings.interpretation: The claims pattern is strong (27% 99215 on 1-condition patients vs 5.6% for peers). The chart rule triggered (2 of 12 below billed) and the notes look inflated (67% address fewer problems than claimed). However, the office did not respond to the follow-up for the 18 missing visits and refused the audit trail. The estimate is unreliable (only 7 charts in the 99214 stratum). Missing records are not evidence. Recommend a person decide on a further request.

findings.headline: 99215 at 6.88x expected on a 65% low-complexity panel; no charts received
findings.interpretation: The strongest claims-only ratio in the book. The office asked for clarification and then did not respond to the follow-up; the request was closed. Non-response is not evidence of upcoding. It cannot be judged without charts, so a human re-contact is suggested.
